reviewer: Owner-delegated automated documentary review with separate automated reviewer
method: Read the 58 current scripts and compare all 27 EN/ES prompt pairs; separately compare source text with current-file local ASR. Review negation, symptoms, numerical meaning, urgency, medication authority, delivery claims and synthetic boundaries. No aggregate word-error score is used as an approval criterion.
findings: 27 EN/ES prompt pairs retain equivalent clinical and synthetic-demo boundaries; four dialogue fixtures are English only.
The 24 outdated recordings were replaced. Four short prompts were additionally regenerated; the English titration emergency prompt was regenerated once more.
Independent automated reconciliation found the clinically consequential content preserved. Lexical and grammatical differences are retained explicitly in each comparison, not erased.
Clinical script acceptance was reported by Rodrigo Costa as Vicky’s acceptance; no direct signature or human listening is represented.
limitations: ASR and documentary comparison cannot certify pronunciation, prosody, accessibility or acoustic intelligibility.
No human listening session is attested.
Synthetic demonstration only; not patient communication, institutional authorization, clinical validation or evidence of delivered care.
